hook: reading National Geographic as a kid to learn about your own Dine culture
how retail plans for even the bestseller to end up marked down
going from 70 employees to fewer than 10, and closing the office two years before the pandemic
the two of you putting in $2,000 each, for a bag to carry a wet bikini
packaging being the one thing you send that has a guaranteed 100% open rate
not knowing a single entrepreneur when you started, and ending up training Wolfgang Puck's staff
the bank manager who'd have financed a car but not your business
noticing how many toothpaste tubes you went through travelling for work
going door to door at CrossFit gyms, then finding out in 2018 your real customer was someone else entirely
a few cans of creamsicle seltzer made to keep festival-goers hydrated turning into 20% of revenue
the all-black packaging and the illustration of a man with a big beard that every men's grooming brand seems to use
the chamomile in the rose that you couldn't explain in copy, people had to taste it
the one-way ticket to Mumbai with $2,000, and paying farmers several times commodity price
asking why anyone should pay $150 just to smell nice on a date
meeting Earl at Morehouse and winning the PGA Minority Collegiate together before any of this existed
being one of the very few businesses actually owned by a tribe
just wanting to stop missing work because of migraines, and prototyping with handwritten labels
rowing being 30 excruciating minutes before you turned it into a game
your grandparents' experience of the famine shaping what you built, in an industry you called known for snake oil
betting on tinned fish in the middle of the pandemic and making the packaging carry the launch
boxing up a farmer friend's produce in a bookstore parking lot and selling 25 boxes that first weekend
the idea coming from a trip to Spain, and olive oil already being in every pantry
hand-tying 20 vintage pendants and DMing every single person who liked a post
launching a candle online where nobody could smell it, so the description had to do all the work
the Christmas sweater launch a week before Christmas, three mistakes in a row as you put it
the idea arriving in the shower, after a winter of getting through a lot of lotion
how tastes shifted region to region, right down to the cut of the clothing
wanting a light that lit only the latch and not the whole room
running out of ideas, and turning that into a collaboration model
treating TikTok Shop as a discovery engine rather than a sales channel
starting on a kitchen stovetop, and spotting that nobody was making a unisex candle
the rainy Yosemite weekend that started it, when everyone else was doing beige on beige
matching blankets to shelters by the customer's own ZIP code
saying outright that you didn't have the capacity to be an overnight success
a stolen bike turning into a lock, and the Kickstarter hitting its goal in six hours
knowing early that the texture was polarizing, and leaning into it anyway
finding out a bigger brand had an internal project called Thousand Killers
being the only beauty brand fully compliant with the National Eczema Association
the 32-ounce bottle that emptied into a tote bag and soaked a laptop
